web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Inside the $403 Billion Engine: Four Segments, One Flywheel
question: Why does McKesson's headline $403 billion revenue mask the real profit engines inside its four operating segments, and what does the company actually deliver at each link of the healthcare chain?

epigraph.quote: Revenue is vanity in drug wholesaling; gross profit dollars and segment operating profit per script are sanity.
epigraph.author: Healthcare Distribution Analyst Principle

web_blocks.html: In FY2026 (ended March 31, 2026), McKesson moved to four operating segments: North American Pharmaceutical, Oncology & Multispecialty, Prescription Technology Solutions (RxTS), and Medical-Surgical Solutions [1, 2]. That shift reflects its North American focus and specialty pivot. Consolidated FY2026 revenue hit $403,430 million (+12% YoY). Adjusted Segment Operating Profit totaled $7,119 million (+16% YoY) before $654 million in net corporate costs [2]. By Q2 FY2027 (ended September 30, 2026), quarterly revenue reached $111.0 billion (+8% YoY), with growth across all four units [5].

The key insight is the sharp gap between revenue share and profit share. North American Pharmaceutical drives 83.4% of revenue ($336.7 billion) at a thin 1.03% adjusted operating margin, yielding 48.5% of segment profit [2]. By contrast, RxTS makes just 1.4% of revenue ($5.8 billion) at a 19.45% margin. That small top line delivers 15.9% of total segment profit [2]. Oncology & Multispecialty sits in the sweet spot. It posted $48.4 billion in revenue (+31% YoY) and $1,435 million in adjusted operating profit (+53% YoY), or 20.2% of segment profits [2].

web_blocks.takeaway: While North American Pharmaceutical drives 83.4% of top-line pass-through revenue, the three higher-margin pillars (Oncology & Multispecialty, RxTS, and Medical-Surgical) generate over 50% of segment operating profit on just 16.3% of revenue.

web_blocks.title: Concrete Real-World Examples Across Every Segment

web_blocks.html: 1. North American Pharmaceutical ($336.7B FY26 revenue): Every weekday morning, McKesson's automated warehouses ship branded, generic, biosimilar, and GLP-1 drugs. They serve over 40,000 U.S. retail pharmacies (including CVS Health, Walmart, and Health Mart), health systems, and Canadian pharmacies [1, 11]. The unit also sells clinical software, 340B compliance tools, and generic sourcing via ClarusONE [1, 22]. In Q2 FY2027, McKesson shipped $16 billion of refrigerated GLP-1 drugs (+26% YoY), managing strict cold-chain custody from factory to local counter [8].

2. Oncology & Multispecialty ($48.4B FY26 revenue): The US Oncology Network supports over 3,400 community cancer providers [8]. When a doctor prescribes a targeted cancer drug, McKesson supplies it, runs Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) pricing, and provides practice software [5, 14]. Through Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) and Precision Medicine Group ($2.25B, closed November 2, 2026), it links patients to biomarker trials in over 30 countries [5, 14]. Through Ontada, McKesson turns clinic records into real-world evidence (RWE) for biopharma R&D [14]. It also applies this model to eye care via PRISM Vision Group (350+ providers after adding Spectrum Vision Partners in November 2026) and Florida Cancer Specialists' Core Ventures [5, 14]. Meanwhile, InspiroGene supports cell and gene therapies [1].

3. Prescription Technology Solutions / RxTS ($5.8B FY26 revenue): Many pricey specialty or GLP-1 drugs need insurer sign-off. CoverMyMeds, McKesson's electronic prior-authorization tool, links doctors, pharmacies, and payers in real time [8]. It covers 96% of U.S. prescription volume, clearing coverage hurdles and applying copay cards [8]. RxTS also offers 3PL and reimbursement support for new drug launches. In Q2 FY2027, RxTS added 67 new biopharma programs across 58 brands and backed the CMS Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program, lifting adjusted operating profit 18% [5, 8].

4. Medical-Surgical Solutions / Wellverse ($11.5B FY26 revenue): McKesson ships gloves, diagnostic kits, IV poles, vaccines, and lab gear to over 260,000 clinics, surgery centers, home-health agencies, and care facilities [1, 5]. Serving fragmented non-hospital sites yields an 8.94% adjusted operating margin [2]. Management is now separating this unit into standalone Wellverse, backed by Apollo Funds' $1.25 billion convertible preferred stake [9].

web_blocks.title: Why Headline Gross Revenue Misleads Amateur Analysts
paragraphs: Branded drugmakers sometimes raise or cut Wholesale Acquisition Cost (WAC). In January 2026, branded WAC cuts shaved ~4% off North American Pharma's Q2 FY2027 revenue growth, yet operating profit barely budged [8].

Likewise, $16 billion per quarter in GLP-1 pass-through volume boosts revenue faster than profit because branded fees are mostly fixed per unit [8, 19]. Segment operating profit dollars—not gross revenue—are the true yardstick of value [8, 19].

web_blocks.html: Together, these four units form a tight flywheel. Core wholesale trucks pay the fixed logistics bill across 40,000 pharmacies [1, 2]. Oncology & Multispecialty and RxTS then ride those same customer ties to capture higher margins [2, 8]. Separating Wellverse sharpens that focus even further [9].

book_paragraphs: When you first open McKesson's income statement, one huge number jumps out: $403.4 billion in annual revenue [2]. That makes McKesson larger by sales than almost every company on Earth except Walmart and Amazon. Yet if you stop there, you will miss how McKesson actually makes money. In drug wholesaling, revenue is mostly a pass-through number. Profit per prescription and segment mix tell the real story.
Let's walk through the four rooms inside McKesson's house. Each room has very different economics, customers, and strategic roles in the flywheel.

The first and largest room is North American Pharmaceutical, which brought in $336.7 billion in fiscal 2026—over 83% of total sales [2]. Picture a climate-controlled warehouse in Texas or Ohio at 4:00 a.m. Robotic pickers sort bottles of blood-pressure pills, generics, and cold GLP-1 pens into blue totes. Those totes head out to CVS stores, Walmart pharmacies, OptumRx hubs, and Health Mart druggists [1, 11, 19]. McKesson buys the drugs, holds them for about three weeks, and delivers overnight. For that feat of logistics, McKesson keeps an adjusted operating margin of just 1.03% [2]. On every $100 of pills, it keeps about $1.03 before interest and taxes. That sounds thin—until you see it is 1.03% on $337 billion, or $3.45 billion in steady profit [2]. Even when drugmakers cut list prices in January 2026 and shaved 4% off segment sales growth, North American Pharma's Q2 profit still jumped 22% [5, 8]. Fees depend on volume and complexity, not sticker price.

Now step into the second room: Oncology & Multispecialty. It generated $48.4 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue (+31% YoY) and $1.44 billion in adjusted operating profit (+53%) [2]. Here, McKesson does far more than drop boxes at a dock. Through The US Oncology Network, it supports over 3,400 community cancer doctors with health records, GPO drug buying, and clinical trial matching via Sarah Cannon and Precision Medicine Group [5, 8, 14]. Picture a patient in Florida or Texas getting an infusion at a local clinic instead of a pricey academic hospital. McKesson supplies the vial, runs the clinic's billing software, captures data via Ontada, and helps biopharma recruit patients for trials [1, 14]. It has even copied this model in eye care through PRISM Vision, now topping 350 providers [5]. Adding Core Ventures and Precision Medicine Group deepens that clinical moat.

The third room is small by revenue—just $5.8 billion, or 1.4% of sales—but it is a profit jewel: Prescription Technology Solutions, or RxTS [2]. Have you ever stood at a pharmacy counter and been told your drug needs 'prior authorization' from your insurer? CoverMyMeds, the heart of RxTS, clears that logjam [8]. Built into doctors' prescribing software and linked to payers covering 96% of U.S. scripts, RxTS automates approvals and applies copay cards in seconds [8]. Because it sells software and data rather than boxes, RxTS earns a 19.45% adjusted operating margin. That is nearly twenty times core wholesaling, generating 16% of McKesson's segment profits [2]. In Q2 FY2027 alone, RxTS added 67 new biopharma programs across 58 brands [8].

The fourth room is Medical-Surgical Solutions, soon to spin off as Wellverse [9]. It posted $11.5 billion in fiscal 2026 shipping gloves, swabs, and lab gear to over 260,000 clinics, urgent-care sites, and nursing homes at an 8.94% margin [1, 2]. By bringing in Apollo Funds for a $1.25 billion stake and separating Wellverse, McKesson lets that unit set its own capital path [9]. Meanwhile, McKesson focuses its balance sheet on North American pharma, oncology, and biopharma services [9]. Watching those three retained engines grow together explains why earnings compound far faster than top-line sales.

Step back and look at how these segments reinforce one another in practice. A community cancer clinic that buys its oncology biologics through McKesson often uses McKesson's practice software too [1, 14]. When that clinic prescribes a new therapy that needs insurer sign-off, CoverMyMeds inside RxTS clears the prior authorization [8]. Every step adds value for the doctor and deepens the relationship for McKesson.

That is also why the January 2026 branded list-price cuts were such a useful real-world test. Even when drugmakers lowered Wholesale Acquisition Cost and shaved 4% off North American Pharma's Q2 revenue growth, segment operating profit still jumped 22% [5, 8]. Volume, cold-chain complexity, and fee-for-service contracts protected McKesson's profit dollars. As investors, we should always track segment operating profit dollars rather than headline revenue.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The secret to reading McKesson is to ignore the $403 billion top-line mirage and follow the profit mix shift. Moving growth from 1%-margin pill wholesaling into 3%-margin oncology MSOs and 19%-margin RxTS software compounds earnings far faster than revenue.
